messages:
emma: quick follow-up from today's RFC. we need a compact playbook for deciding when to carve a tenant out from the regional shared gateway to a dedicated gateway. goal: minimize ops burden but meet compliance needs.

li: short summary: carve-out triggers = preserve_srcip requirement, dedicated certs/SNI passthrough, >2k rps sustained for 24h, or explicit enterprise contract. keep the default as shared slices.

otto: ops concerns: carving too eagerly will exhaust IP space. we should require a small review step for non-contract carve requests and document an emergency carve path.

marta: compatibility: connectors will send routing.contract.v1 with egress_profile enum. controller decides placement. older connectors default to shared. add a header warning for connectors that lack the field so SDKs can surface migration hints.

emma: allocator behavior: allocate labeled blocks (slice-id:/28) to slices, track ledger with version stamps, and keep a global reserve of /24 per-region for emergencies. set alert ippool.utilization > 65%.

li: DNS handling: routing controller will push tenant-specific private records for private endpoints. use per-tenant stamps so updates are idempotent and diffs-only. avoids flapping.

otto: fallback plan: if shared gateway capacity falters, automated per-tenant route reversion to dedicated pool for affected tenants. define p99 latency threshold and rollback window.

marta: telemetry: emit egress.ip_changes, allocation_age, and mapping.mode per-tenant. console should provide a small graph for egress churn.

emma: action items:
- emma: write the operator playbook for carve-out + emergency path (due Fri)
- li: add egress_profile enum to routing.contract.v1 and validation rules (PR Tue)
- otto: design allocator ledger + reserve policy (doc Wed)
- marta: telemetry fields + dashboard mock (PR Wed)

infra-bot: routing-slice-controller canary deployment started in staging (build ci-5412) 

emma: i'll update the RFC with these decisions and the playbook link when ready. keep updates here. :thumbsup:
